name: York stone (Carboniferous sandstone flags, West Yorkshire)

diffuseAlbedo.note: A first colour for York stone (Carboniferous sandstone flags, West Yorkshire): no measured colour was read: a first value read from trade and museum photographs of the named material.

refractiveIndex.source: Handbook of Mineralogy, Quartz (Anthony, Bideaux, Bladh and Nichols, Mineralogical Society of America): n omega 1.544
refractiveIndex.note: The ordinary index of the quartz grains that make most of a sandstone.

porosity.source: Marshalls plc data sheets. 'Howley Park Yorkstone Blue/Grey' (created 28/01/25; Thornhill sandstone sequence, Howley Park, West Yorkshire): open porosity 13.90 % (mean, EN 1936:2006), density 2339 kg/m3, water absorption 4.5 % (EN 13755). 'Scoutmoor Yorkstone' (created 12/03/25; Millstone Grit and Westphalian A sandstone, Appleton Quarry, Yorkshire and Whitworth Quarry, Lancashire): open porosity 10.82 % (EN 1936:2006), density 2389 kg/m3, water absorption 2.29 %. https://docs.planning.org.uk/20260416/31/TCRT03BK12200/uzzfiyfhe0hv98iw.pdf and https://www.externalworksindex.co.uk/Docs/1765277226161/preview/Scoutmoor-Yorkstone-paving-data-sheet.pdf
porosity.note: Both values were confirmed on the sheets. Scoutmoor is partly quarried in Lancashire (Whitworth), outside the record's West Yorkshire. If the record should stay strictly West Yorkshire, use the Howley Park value, 0.139 (manufacturer). Either way, 11 to 14 % replaces the unverified 7 %.
porosity.derivation: mean of two manufacturer EN 1936 open porosities: (0.1390 + 0.1082)/2 = 0.1236, rounded to 0.124

wettingDepth.note: The depth whose pores govern the face's look when wet.

grain.note: The finest structure the face shows at gallery distance.

bed.note: The flags split along thin bedding planes a few centimetres apart.

bedAspect.note: How much longer the structure runs along its bedding than across it.

hurst.source: Candela et al. 2012, J. Geophys. Res. Solid Earth 117, B08409, doi:10.1029/2011JB009041, abstract (read via https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1029/2011JB009041).
hurst.note: The exponents are confirmed. This is a transfer from fracture surfaces to a sawn and trodden sandstone flag.

toneSpread.note: A first half-range of ln(albedo) across one face.

roughnessSpread.note: A first half-range of ln(roughness) across one face.
